Reflection summary:

The error was a definitional one, not a parsing slip. The question asked for the **RELATIVE difference** of the savings-note redemption rate between 1980 and 1981. I computed the **absolute** percentage-point gap (3.85) instead of normalizing: gold 17.69 = |r1980 − r1981| / base × 100. Off by a ~1/base factor (~4.6x), with all underlying digits otherwise fine.

This is generalizable because OfficeQA mixes "absolute difference" / "difference in percentage points" (plain |A−B|) with "relative difference" / "percent difference" (|A−B|/base×100), and the existing share-ratio reference only covered the absolute-difference case. A future agent that grabbed that procedure would make exactly my mistake.

Saved:
- New reference `relative-vs-absolute-difference.md` — decision rule (scan for the literal word "relative"), the normalize formula, base-selection guidance, and the savings-note "redemption rate out of average amount outstanding" = redemptions/avg-outstanding definition.
- A pointer line in SKILL.md (via filesystem patch, since the file is >100KB and skill_manage patch is blocked).

No memory update needed — this is procedural and lives better in the skill reference than in the compact memory store.
